mainTopic: ציצית: the meaning of 'פטורה', folded cloaks, whether ציצית is a duty on the person or the garment, and repairing a torn טלית
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about how big a garment must be to need ציצית. The ברייתא shows that a garment too small for ציצית is still bound by כלאים. So 'פטורה' in שמואל's statement must mean adding ציצית to a garment that already has them. Next, a ברייתא and a story about רבא בר רב נחמן deal with a folded cloak, and when the corners made by a fold count. רבה בר הונא then teaches that ציצית is a duty on the garment (חובת טלית), not only on the person wearing it. The גמרא tests this against an angel who scolded רב קטינא for dodging ציצית, and concludes that the angel held the duty is on the person. שמואל rules that garments stored in a box need ציצית, but a shroud is exempt. Even so, we attach ציצית at burial out of respect for the dead. The amud ends with the rules for sewing a torn טלית near its corner and for taking ציצית from elsewhere.

steps.title: The ברייתא on the Minimum Size of a Tallit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a garment big enough for a child to cover his head and most of his body needs ציצית, and a smaller one is exempt. It adds that the same applies to כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and an adult sometimes goes out wearing it: it needs ציצית. If a child cannot cover his head and most of his body with it, it is exempt, even if an adult sometimes goes out in it. The same applies to כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that sets the minimum size for a garment to need ציצית. It brings this source to test what 'פטורה' could mean in שמואל's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is the child: if a child can cover his head and most of his body with it, the garment needs ציצית. If not, it is exempt, even if an adult sometimes wears it outside. The last line, 'the same applies to כלאים,' seems to suggest that a small garment is also free of כלאים, and that is what the next steps examine.

keyTerms.meaning: Fringes the תורה requires on a four-cornered garment
His head and most of his body
Forbidden mixture; here, wool and linen together in clothing

steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a ברייתא. The opening words are only the end of the rule. The full rule is: a garment a child can cover his head and most of his body with, which an adult also sometimes wears outside, needs ציצית.

phrases.english: and an adult goes out in it occasionally –
phrases.notes: This continues a ברייתא that began just before: a garment that a child can cover his head and most of his body with.

phrases.english: it is required to have fringes,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּטָן מִתְכַּסֶּה בּוֹ רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ,
phrases.english: if a child cannot cover his head and most of his body with it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַגָּדוֹל יוֹצֵא בָּהּ עֲרַאי –
phrases.english: even though an adult goes out in it occasionally –
it is exempt,
and the same applies to diverse kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא quoted just before this section, used to test the meaning of 'פטורה'.
steps.raayaObject: Whether 'פטורה' in שמואל's statement could mean a garment too small to need ציצית
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא setting the minimum size of a טלית for ציצית
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'פטורה' in שמואל's statement means a garment too small to need ציצית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's line 'וכן לענין כלאים' (as explained in step 4) teaches that wool ציצית on a garment too small for ציצית is forbidden כלאים, so a small garment cannot be the 'exempt' garment that is free of כלאים.

steps.title: What Does 'The Same Applies to כלאים' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that it once asked what the ברייתא's last line means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: what does 'and the same applies to כלאים' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's closing line about כלאים really means. This sets up the next move, where one possible reading is tried and rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line is unclear. Does it mean a small garment is not subject to the כלאים prohibition at all, or does it mean something else about כלאים? The answer will decide whether this ברייתא supports reading 'פטורה' as a small garment.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (an earlier discussion is being recalled)

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is meant by 'and the same applies to diverse kinds'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last line of the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'וכן לענין כלאים' in the ברייתא

steps.title: כלאים Has No Leniency for Occasional Wear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the line means a small garment is free of the כלאים prohibition, then rejects this from a משנה: 'אין עראי בכלאים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the כלאים prohibition does not apply to a small garment, that cannot be. We learned in a משנה: there is no leniency for occasional wear with כלאים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple reading: a garment too small for ציצית is also free of the כלאים prohibition. It immediately attacks this reading with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that even clothing worn only occasionally is still forbidden as כלאים. So the size or usage of a garment does not remove the כלאים prohibition. The simple reading of the ברייתא therefore cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)
Occasional wear is no excuse when it comes to כלאים

phrases.english: If you say: and the same applies to the prohibition of diverse kinds,
phrases.notes: Meaning a garment too small for ציצית would also be free of the wool-and-linen prohibition.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn in a mishna:
phrases.notes: כלאים 9:2

phrases.english: there is no 'occasional' with diverse kinds!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן אִיסּוּרָא דְכִלְאַיִם וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers one answer to the question in step 2 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that a small garment is free of the כלאים prohibition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says the כלאים prohibition applies even to clothing worn only occasionally, so a garment's smallness cannot remove it.

steps.title: It Means a Linen Garment with Wool Fringes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the line is about putting wool ציצית on a linen garment (סדין בציצית).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it means the same rule applies to a linen garment with ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the correct meaning of the ברייתא's last line. It is about whether a linen garment may get wool ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A linen garment that is big enough to need ציצית may get wool ציצית, because the מצוה allows the mixture. A garment too small to need ציצית may not get wool ציצית, since that would be plain כלאים. So a small garment is not freed from כלאים. If anything, it is the case where כלאים is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that being too small for ציצית leads to more strictness about כלאים, not less. That point decides the meaning of 'פטורה' in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
and the same applies to a linen cloak with fringes.
phrases.notes: If it is big enough to need ציצית, wool fringes are allowed on it. If it is too small, they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן סָדִין בְּצִיצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer to step 2 after step 3 rejected the simple reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's line means that only a garment big enough for ציצית may have wool ציצית on linen; a small one may not.

steps.title: 'Exempt' Means Adding Fringes to an Already-Fringed Garment
steps.stepSummary: Since a small garment is not freed from כלאים, 'פטורה' in שמואל's statement must mean adding ציצית to a garment that already has ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'exempt' mean? He attached ציצית to a garment that already had ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main question about the word 'פטורה' in שמואל's statement. It concludes that the word means adding ציצית to a garment that already has them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that a small garment does not escape כלאים, so 'פטורה' cannot mean a small garment. Instead it describes a garment that already has its ציצית and so has no further obligation. According to the statement, adding a second set of wool ציצית to such a linen garment is still not a כלאים violation.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier idea and gives a new one)
He attached ציצית to a garment that already had ציצית

steps.whatToRemember: A garment too small for ציצית is still bound by כלאים, so wool ציצית may not go on it. Therefore 'פטורה' in שמואל's statement means a garment that already has ציצית, where adding another set is still not כלאים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'פטורה' here as 'too small to need ציצית.' The גמרא just ruled that out. It means 'already has its ציצית.'

phrases.english: Rather, what is meant by 'exempt'?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the word 'exempt' in שמואל's statement, discussed before this section.

phrases.english: He attached fringes to one that already had fringes attached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 4 to settle the main question of what 'פטורה' means.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'פטורה' means attaching ציצית to a garment that already has ציצית. Even that extra set is not a כלאים violation, while a garment too small for ציצית is fully bound by כלאים.

steps.title: Didn't רבי זירא already say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי זירא already said this rule once, so why does it show up again?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי זירא already say this one time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the conclusion just reached (adding ציצית to a garment that already has ציצית) sounds like something רבי זירא already said. It asks why he would say the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 read 'פטורה' as being about adding ציצית to a garment that already has them. But רבי זירא already taught a rule about that same case. A sage does not usually repeat himself, so the double statement needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, but isn't it that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't רבי זירא say it
phrases.notes: He means רבי זירא's earlier rule about a garment that already had ציצית, where the first set of strings was later removed.

phrases.english: one time already?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַמְרַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 5 because it makes רבי זירא repeat himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'פטורה' reached in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that reading is right, רבי זירא said the same rule twice, and a sage would not repeat himself for no reason.

steps.title: One statement was worked out from the other
steps.stepSummary: Answer: רבי זירא said only one of them. The other was learned from it by inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was stated by inference from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא did not really say both statements. He said one, and the other was inferred from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real repetition, because only one statement came from רבי זירא himself. The second is something people learned from what he said and then recorded as if it were its own statement. So step 5's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: From the implication of, by inference

phrases.english: One was stated by inference from the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the statement was passed down: only one statement is original
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא seemed to have said the same rule twice
steps.terutzMaskana: He said one, and the other was inferred from it, so there is no repetition
steps.whatToRemember: The reading of 'פטורה' as adding ציצית to a garment that already has ציצית stands. The apparent double statement of רבי זירא is really one statement plus an inference from it.

steps.title: A ברייתא on a folded cloak
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a folded cloak needs ציצית at the fold, רבי שמעון exempts it, and all agree a folded and sewn cloak needs them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: a folded cloak must have ציצית, and רבי שמעון exempts it. They agree that if he folded it and sewed it, it must have ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about a long cloak folded in half. It asks whether the corners made by the fold need ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the fold counts and needs ציצית there. רבי שמעון says it is exempt, because the fold is not one of the garment's real corners. Both agree that once the fold is sewn closed, it does need ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: A folded cloak (a long garment doubled over)
He folded it and sewed it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A folded cloak must have ציצית,
phrases.notes: Meaning ציצית on the corners made by the fold.

phrases.english: and רבי שמעון exempts it,
and they agree that if he folded it and sewed it
it must have them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: טַלִּית כְּפוּלָה חַיֶּיבֶת בְּצִיצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Folded cloak: the Rabbis require ציצית at the fold and רבי שמעון exempts it. If folded and sewn, all require ציצית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of when a fold counts as a real corner, which the story that follows puts into practice.

steps.title: Why say the sewn case at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: of course a sewn cloak needs ציצית, so why does the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sewed it, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothered to say that a folded and sewn cloak needs ציצית, since that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the fold is sewn closed, the folded edge becomes the garment's real edge, so of course it needs ציצית. Saying something obvious seems pointless, so the גמרא asks what new point is being taught.

phrases.english: If he sewed it, that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the last clause of the ברייתא in step 8 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause 'ושוין שאם כפלה ותפרה שחייבת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sewn fold is clearly a permanent part of the garment, so the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: It means a cloak held with pins
steps.stepSummary: Answer: 'sewed' here means he only fastened the fold with pins, and even then everyone agrees ציצית are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he fastened it with pins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not talking about real sewing. It means a fold that is only held in place with pins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pins are not a strong or permanent way to close a fold, so you might think the fold does not count. The ברייתא teaches that even pinning is enough for everyone, including רבי שמעון, to require ציצית. That is a new point, so the clause is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (the ruling teaches a less obvious case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'ותפרה' in the ברייתא as normal sewing. The גמרא explains it as fastening with pins, which is why the clause teaches something new.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he fastened it with pins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (pins rather than real sewing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause seemed to be about real sewing, which would be obvious
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about pins, and even that much fastening makes everyone agree ציצית are required
steps.whatToRemember: A folded cloak: חכמים require ציצית at the fold and רבי שמעון exempts it. If the fold is fastened, even only with pins, everyone requires them.

steps.title: The story of the folded cloak that came open
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא sees רבא בר רב נחמן wearing a folded cloak with strings on the fold. It comes unfolded and a string ends up by his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר הונא came to the house of רבא בר רב נחמן. He saw that he was wearing a folded cloak and had put strings on the fold. The cloak came unfolded, and a string came and settled near his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that shows the folded-cloak case in real life. This step sets up the scene, and the reaction to it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר רב נחמן followed the view that the fold needs ציצית, so he put strings on the corners made by the fold. When the cloak opened up, those strings were no longer at a corner. One of them ended up in the middle, near his head. This sets up the problem the story will deal with next.

phrases.english: רבה בר הונא came
to the house of רבא בר רב נחמן,
he saw that he was wearing
a folded cloak,
and he had put strings on it at the fold.
It came unfolded,
and the string came
and settled near his head.
phrases.notes: Once the cloak opened, that string was in the middle of the garment, not at any corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר הוּנָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא בַּר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life case of the folded cloak discussed in the ברייתא of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: a folded cloak with strings on the fold came open, leaving a string in the middle of the garment. The ruling comes in the next part of the story.

steps.title: A fold is not a real corner, so he switches cloaks
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא points out that the string at the fold is not on the corner the תורה means. רבא בר רב נחמן takes off that cloak and puts on a different one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is not the corner the תורה is talking about! So he took it off and wrapped himself in a different cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step continues. רבה בר הונא objects that the string near רבא בר רב נחמן's head is not on a real corner, so רבא בר רב נחמן swaps cloaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the cloak came unfolded, the strings that had been tied at the fold were no longer at a true corner of the garment. רבא בר רב נחמן's quick fix is to stop wearing that cloak. That fix sets up רבה בר הונא's next comment.

keyTerms.meaning: Corner of a garment, the place where the Torah requires ציצית
The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah

phrases.english: He said to him: This is not the corner
phrases.notes: רבה בר הונא is speaking to רבא בר רב נחמן.

phrases.english: that the Merciful One wrote in the Torah!
He went and threw it off,
and covered himself with a different cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ כָּנָף דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the folded cloak from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strings at a fold do not count as ציצית on the Torah's corner once the garment is opened.

steps.title: ציצית is a duty on the garment, not only on the wearer
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא tells רבא בר רב נחמן that switching cloaks does not solve the problem. ציצית is a duty on the garment, so he must put proper ציצית on the first cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think ציצית is a duty on the man? It is a duty on the garment. Go put ציצית on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר הונא rejects the idea that just taking off the cloak solves things, and orders proper ציצית put on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ציצית were only חובת גברא, a duty that applies when a person wears a garment, then not wearing the cloak would end the problem. רבה בר הונא holds it is חובת טלית, a duty on every four-cornered garment a person owns, worn or not. So the unworn cloak still needs ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: A duty on the person, which applies only when he wears the garment
A duty on the garment itself, even when it is not being worn

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the passage: is ציצית a duty on the person or on the garment? The rest of this section tests רבה בר הונא's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה בר הונא is objecting to the new cloak. His point is that the old cloak still needs ציצית even after it is taken off.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
it is an obligation on the man?
It is an obligation on the garment,
go and put them on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ חוֹבַת גַּבְרָא הוּא? חוֹבַת טַלִּית הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבא בר רב נחמן's switching cloaks in step 12 and turns the story into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבה בר הונא, ציצית is חובת טלית, so even a garment that is not being worn needs ציצית.

steps.title: A possible proof from the early pious men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports רבה בר הונא. The early חסידים put תכלת on a garment as soon as three fingerbreadths of it had been woven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? The early pious men, once they had woven three fingerbreadths of a garment, would attach תכלת to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the early חסידים to try to prove רבה בר הונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garment still on the loom is not being worn by anyone. If the חסידים attached תכלת to it anyway, it looks like the duty belongs to the garment itself, which is חובת טלית.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him? This opens a suggested proof
The early pious men of earlier generations

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה בר הונא, who said ציצית is a duty on the garment.

phrases.english: The early pious men,
once they had woven three of it
phrases.notes: Three fingerbreadths of the garment's length, while it was still being made.

phrases.english: would put תכלת on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support the rule from step 13 with an earlier source.
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר הונא's view that ציצית is חובת טלית
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying the early חסידים attached תכלת to a garment that was still being woven

steps.title: The pious men were simply extra strict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. חסידים are different because they take on extra strictness, so their practice does not show what the law requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: Pious men are different, because they are strict with themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What extra-careful people do beyond the letter of the law cannot prove what is required of everyone. So the ברייתא does not show that ציצית is חובת טלית.

keyTerms.meaning: They are strict with themselves, going beyond what is required

phrases.english: Pious men are different,
since they are strict with themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רבה בר הונא's view itself is not refuted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The practice of חסידים reflects personal strictness, not the basic law.

steps.title: An angel's words suggest the opposite view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבה בר הונא's view seems to disagree with an angel. The angel scolded רב קטינא for wearing garments that never required ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with the angel. An angel found רב קטינא wearing a linen cloak and said to him: קטינא, קטינא! A linen cloak in summer and a coat in winter, what will become of the מצוה of ציצית of תכלת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about an angel and רב קטינא that seems to clash with רבה בר הונא's view that ציצית is a duty on the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel complains that רב קטינא picks clothing that never obligates him in ציצית, so he will miss the מצוה. That complaint only makes sense if ציצית depends on what a person wears, which is חובת גברא, and not on the garments he owns.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with the angel,
phrases.notes: "This" is רבה בר הונא's view that ציצית is a duty on the garment.

phrases.english: for an angel found Rav Ketina
wearing a linen cloak,
He said to him: Ketina, Ketina!
A linen cloak in the summer
and a coat in the winter,

phrases.aramaic: צִיצִית שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת מָה תְּהֵא עָלֶיהָ?
phrases.english: ציצית of תכלת, what will become of it?
phrases.notes: The angel is saying that with these clothes, you will never end up doing the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבה בר הונא's rule from step 13 and shows a source that seems to hold the opposite view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angel's rebuke suggests that ציצית is חובת גברא, a duty that depends on what a person chooses to wear.

steps.title: רב קטינא asks if one is punished for skipping a positive מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא asks the angel whether people are punished just for not doing a מצות עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said to the angel: Do you punish people for failing to do a positive commandment?
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step continues. רב קטינא answers the angel's rebuke with a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not wearing ציצית is only a failure to do something, a עשה. It is not doing a forbidden act. רב קטינא is surprised that this kind of failure would bring heavenly punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment, a מצוה to actively do something

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you punish for a positive commandment?
phrases.notes: רב קטינא is speaking to the angel from the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation between the angel and רב קטינא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether failing to keep a positive commandment brings punishment

steps.title: The angel says punishment comes in a time of anger
steps.stepSummary: The angel answers that at a time of divine anger, people are punished even for skipping a עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The angel said to him: At a time when there is divine anger, we do punish.
steps.whatsHappening: The angel answers רב קטינא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, failing to do a עשה may not bring punishment. But when there is heavenly anger and judgment, even this kind of failure is held against a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Anger, a time of divine judgment

phrases.english: He said to him:
At a time when there is anger, we punish.
phrases.notes: This time it is the angel speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב קטינא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a time of divine anger, people are punished even for failing to do a positive commandment

steps.title: The story seems to fit only the view that ציצית is a duty on the person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the angel's rebuke makes sense only if ציצית is a חובת גברא. If it is a חובת טלית, as רבה בר הונא holds, רב קטינא's garments did not need ציצית at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say ציצית is a duty on the man, because then he is liable for not putting ציצית on. But if you say it is a duty on the garment, his garment was not obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the angel story to challenge רבה בר הונא's view that ציצית is a חובת טלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the duty is on the person, you could say רב קטינא failed his own duty, so he deserved punishment. If the duty is on the garment, his garments needed nothing, so there is no reason to punish him. The angel's rebuke therefore seems to go against רבה בר הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: A duty on the person: the man must wear ציצית
A duty on the garment: any garment of the right kind must have ציצית

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא חוֹבַת גַּבְרָא הוּא –
phrases.english: It works well if you say it is a duty on the man,
that is why he is liable, since he does not put on ציצית.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ חוֹבַת טַלִּית הוּא –
phrases.english: But if you say it is a duty on the garment,
this garment is not obligated!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא חוֹבַת גַּבְרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the angel story into a challenge against רבה בר הונא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר הונא's view that ציצית is a חובת טלית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The angel punished רב קטינא for garments that did not need ציצית. That only makes sense if the duty is on the person.

steps.title: Even a duty on the person would not cover a garment that is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even if ציצית is a חובת גברא, the Torah only obligates a person when he wears a garment that needs ציצית, not an exempt one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, if it is a duty on the man? Granted the תורה obligated him when he wears a garment that needs ציצית. But when he wears a garment that does not need ציצית, did the תורה obligate him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the challenge. It shows the angel's words do not fit the other view any better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the duty is on the person, it only applies when he wears a four-cornered garment. רב קטינא wore exempt garments, so even under חובת גברא he broke no rule. So why was he threatened with punishment? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
Subject to the obligation, a garment that needs ציצית

phrases.english: Rather, what, if it is a duty on the man?
Granted that the Merciful One obligated him
when he wears a garment that is subject to the obligation,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִיכַּסֵּי טַלִּית דְּלָאו בַּת חִיּוּבָא הִיא,
phrases.english: but when he wears a garment that is not subject to the obligation,
did the Merciful One obligate him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 19's explanation: even under חובת גברא, wearing exempt garments creates no liability, so the angel's threat needs explaining.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference from the angel story against רבה בר הונא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even under חובת גברא, an exempt garment creates no duty, so the story cannot tell the two views apart.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חובת גברא means a man must always wear a four-cornered garment. Even on this view, the duty begins only when he actually wears one.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 19's claim that under חובת גברא רב קטינא was liable for not attaching ציצית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah obligates a man only when he wears a garment that needs ציצית. רב קטינא's garments did not need ציצית, so he had no obligation even under חובת גברא.

steps.title: The angel meant: you are using tricks to avoid ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the angel's real point. רב קטינא was not technically liable, but he was criticized for using ploys to exempt himself from ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the angel said to him: Are you using tricks to exempt yourself from ציצית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true meaning of the angel's rebuke, which ends the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel was not saying the law required ציצית on those garments. He was criticizing רב קטינא for choosing garments on purpose to dodge the מצוה, which is punished in a time of divine anger. This kind of dodging is only possible if the duty depends on what you wear (חובת גברא), so the angel's view still differs from רבה בר הונא's.
steps.whatToRemember: The angel's complaint was that רב קטינא was dodging the מצוה on purpose by choosing exempt clothing. That complaint only makes sense if ציצית is חובת גברא. So the angel really does disagree with רבה בר הונא, as the גמרא said in step 16.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that even when something is technically allowed, deliberately running away from a מצוה can be judged harshly in a time of divine anger.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he said to him:
Tricks to exempt yourself from ציצית?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-reads the angel's rebuke after showing it cannot be a technical liability
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The angel was punishing a real legal failure to put ציצית on his garments.
steps.terutzMaskana: The angel was criticizing רב קטינא for deliberately avoiding the מצוה, not for breaking the law. That criticism fits חובת גברא, so the angel disagrees with רבה בר הונא.

steps.title: Stored garments need ציצית, but an old man's shroud does not
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that garments kept in a box need ציצית, but he agrees that a garment made as a shroud for an old man is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי בר קיסנא said in the name of שמואל: garments kept in a box must have ציצית. But שמואל agrees that a garment an old man made in his honor, as his shroud, is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of שמואל: a four-cornered garment needs ציצית even while it sits unused in a box. He then names one exception, a burial shroud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If stored garments need ציצית even when no one is wearing them, the obligation must rest on the garment itself. This matches the חובת טלית view that רבה בר הונא taught in step 13. The shroud is the exception: even on that view, this garment is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Garments stored in a box, not being worn
For his honor (here, a burial shroud)

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the box makes a person obligated. The point is that the garment itself needs ציצית even when no one is wearing it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear source for the view that ציצית is a חובת טלית, which ties back to the debate in steps 19-21.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Tovi bar Kisna said that Shmuel said:
Garments kept in a box are obligated in ritual fringes,
but Shmuel agrees in the case of an old man
who made it in his honor, that it is exempt.
phrases.notes: "In his honor" means he prepared it as his own burial shroud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling that relates to the חובת טלית / חובת גברא question raised in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stored garments need ציצית. A shroud made for an old man is exempt.

steps.title: Why the shroud is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the exemption from the פסוק "אשר תכסה בה": a shroud is not made for covering oneself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The תורה says "with which you cover yourself," and this shroud is not made for covering oneself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל exempts the shroud and answers from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the obligation is on the garment, the תורה only requires ציצית on a garment meant to be worn by a living person. A shroud is not that kind of garment, so it falls outside the מצוה altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: "With which you cover yourself" (the פסוק about ציצית)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The Merciful One said "with which you cover yourself,"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:12

phrases.english: and this is not made for covering oneself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the exception named in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק limits ציצית to garments made for covering oneself, and a shroud is not one of them.

steps.title: At burial we still attach ציצית
steps.stepSummary: Even though a shroud is technically exempt, at the time of burial we attach ציצית so as not to mock the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time, the burial, we certainly attach ציצית to it, because of the פסוק "Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a practical point. The shroud is exempt by law, but at the funeral we put ציצית on it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burying a man without ציצית would be like taunting him that he can no longer do מצוות. So the ציצית are attached out of respect for the dead, not because the תורה requires them on the shroud.

keyTerms.meaning: One who mocks the poor (here applied to the dead)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 22. The shroud is still exempt by law. The ציצית are added only because of כבוד המת, the honor of the dead.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between a garment's legal status and how we act out of respect.

phrases.english: At that time, we certainly attach them to it,
phrases.notes: "That time" is the burial, and "them" means the ציצית.

phrases.english: because of "Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker."
phrases.notes: משלי 17:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how the exemption from steps 22-23 plays out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At burial we attach ציצית to the shroud so as not to mock the dead.
steps.whatToRemember: Stored garments need ציצית (חובת טלית). A shroud is exempt because it is not for covering oneself, but at burial we attach ציצית anyway out of respect.

steps.title: Sewing a טלית that tore near its corner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that a tear more than three fingerbreadths from the edge may be sewn, but a tear within three may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה said in the name of רבי יהודה: if a טלית tore, and the tear is more than three fingerbreadths from the edge, one may sew it. If it is within three, one may not sew it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: what to do when a טלית with ציצית tears near one of its corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line is drawn at three fingerbreadths from the edge, close to where the ציצית hang. A tear farther in may be sewn. A tear inside that zone may not, and the text does not give the reason here.

phrases.english: Raḥava said that Rabbi Yehuda said:
A cloak that became torn:
beyond three, one may sew it;
phrases.notes: "Three" means three fingerbreadths from the edge of the garment.

phrases.english: within three, one may not sew it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, sewing a torn טלית, unrelated to the shroud discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tear beyond three fingerbreadths may be sewn. A tear within three may not.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ruling and shows a dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule, showing that רבי יהודה's ruling follows רבי מאיר, while חכמים allow sewing even within three.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: if a טלית tore, beyond three fingerbreadths one may sew it. Within three, רבי מאיר says one may not sew it, and חכמים say one may sew it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יהודה's ruling. It also shows that the case within three fingerbreadths is a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a tear beyond three may be sewn. Within three, רבי מאיר forbids sewing, and that is the ruling רבי יהודה gave in step 25. חכמים allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: This was also taught (in a ברייתא), bringing support

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא supports רבי יהודה's wording, but that does not make it the only opinion. חכמים disagree about a tear within three.

phrases.english: This was also taught in a baraita:
A cloak that became torn:
beyond three, one may sew it;

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹךְ שָׁלֹשׁ – רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִתְפּוֹר,
phrases.english: within three, Rabbi Meir says: one may not sew it,
and the Rabbis say: one may sew it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 25 with a ברייתא and shows that רבי יהודה's ruling matches רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling about sewing a torn טלית
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that records the same rule as רבי מאיר's view, with חכמים disagreeing about a tear within three
steps.whatToRemember: A tear beyond three fingerbreadths may be sewn according to everyone. Within three, רבי מאיר (and רבי יהודה) forbid sewing, while חכמים permit it.

steps.title: Both agree: no attaching a patch that already has ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that רבי מאיר and חכמים both agree that a piece of cloth with תכלת on it, even a large one, may not be brought from elsewhere and attached to a garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both sides agree that a person may not bring a piece of cloth from somewhere else, even one a cubit by a cubit, that already has תכלת on it, and attach it to the garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from what רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about to something they both agree on. You cannot sew on a patch that already has ציצית on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the two sides argued about sewing a torn corner. Here they agree that the strings must be tied onto the garment itself, not onto a separate cloth that is then attached. The word 'even' tells us that a large patch, a full אמה square, is still not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree. Here it means רבי מאיר and חכמים hold the same view.
A cubit by a cubit, a fairly large square piece of cloth
Attaches or hangs it onto the garment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is that the patch is too small. Even a big patch is not allowed. The issue is that the ציצית were not tied onto the garment itself.

phrases.english: And they agree that one may not bring
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי מאיר and חכמים from the previous step. Even though they argued there, they agree on this.

phrases.english: even a cubit by a cubit
from another place, with תכלת on it,
and attach it to the garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 26 and adds a point both sides agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A piece of cloth that already has ציצית on it may not be attached to a garment, even if it is a cubit square.

steps.title: Both agree: strings themselves may be taken from elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that both sides agree a person may take תכלת strings from another place and attach them to the garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both sides agree that a person may bring תכלת strings from somewhere else and attach them to the garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second point that רבי מאיר and חכמים agree on. Taking the strings from elsewhere is fine, as long as you tie them directly onto the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of step 27. There, a patch that already had ציצית was not allowed. Here, the strings alone may come from another place, such as another garment. The strings do not have to be new. What matters is that they are tied directly onto this garment.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings, meaning one is allowed to bring
From another place, for example from a different garment

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree: a patch that already has ציצית on it may not be attached. Loose ציצית strings taken from elsewhere may be tied on. The strings must be tied directly to the garment itself.

phrases.english: And they agree that one may bring תכלת
phrases.notes: Here תכלת means the strings by themselves, with no piece of cloth attached.

phrases.english: from another place and attach it to the garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second point of agreement that contrasts with step 27: strings alone may be taken from elsewhere, but a patch with ציצית may not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית strings may be taken from another place and tied directly onto a garment.
